overview.intro:
Chapter 96 is the catch-all chapter for everyday manufactured goods: **brooms, brushes and toothbrushes, buttons and zippers, pens, pencils and crayons, lighters, combs and hair clips, vacuum flasks and insulated tumblers, mannequins, tripods, and diapers, sanitary pads and tampons** (heading 9619), plus worked ivory, bone and shell and empty capsules. 128 of its 157 tariff lines carry a base duty, mostly **2%–10%**; the highest are brooms over their annual quantity (32¢ each or 32%), synthetic textile diapers (16%) and plastic or coil zippers (13%). Disposable diapers and pads of paper pulp, toothbrushes, makeup brushes and pen nibs are Free.

The U.S. imported **$8.27B** of these goods in 2025: **China** $4.08B (49%), then Canada and Mexico (mostly diapers and pads, Free under USMCA), Japan (pens and markers) and Vietnam. On top of the base rate comes an **extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — **+10%** for India, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia and the UK, **+12.5%** for Vietnam and Thailand, **10% in total** for EU goods and 12.5% in total for Japan and Korea. **China pays +12.5% plus its 2018–2019 list duty**: +25% on buttons, zippers and tripods (List 3) and +7.5% on most pens, pencils, brushes, lighters and diapers (List 4A) — a Chinese zipper pays up to 50.5%. **Cased pencils from China** also owe a 114.90% antidumping duty. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico pay nothing extra, and no Chapter 96 line is on the Canada Section 338 lists. Lighters must meet **CPSC child-resistance standards**, and tampons and menstrual pads are **FDA-regulated medical devices**.

productGroups.label: Worked ivory, bone, horn, shell, coral & mother-of-pearl
productGroups.blurb: Worked ivory, worked shell and articles of bone, horn, hoof or whalebone are Free; coral and cameos for jewelry pay 2.1%, other worked animal carving material such as mother-of-pearl 3.7%. Worked shell (9601.90.20) is on the general Section 301 exemption list (note 52(b)). African elephant ivory cannot be imported commercially, whalebone and other marine-mammal products are barred, and CITES species (hawksbill tortoiseshell, black coral) need permits.

productGroups.label: Gelatin & vegetable capsules, wax figures, amber & other carvings
productGroups.blurb: Empty gelatin capsules pay 3%, empty vegetable (cellulose) capsules 2.7%, molded or carved wax articles 1.8%, and articles of amber, jet, corozo or other vegetable or mineral carving material 2.7%. India and Mexico are the largest suppliers.

productGroups.label: Brooms, brushes, toothbrushes, makeup brushes, paint rollers & mops
productGroups.blurb: Toothbrushes, makeup and artists' brushes over 5¢ each, feather dusters and brushes for machines are Free. Hairbrushes pay 0.2¢ each + 7% (up to 40¢) or 0.3¢ each + 3.6%, paint rollers 7.5%, paint brushes and pads 4%, mops and other brooms 2.8%. Brooms of broomcorn pay 8% on the first 121,478 dozen entered each calendar year (61,655 dozen for whiskbrooms), then 32¢ each or 32%.

productGroups.label: Hand sieves & riddles
productGroups.blurb: Hand sieves and hand riddles pay 4.9%; sieves that are parts of machines are classified with the machine.

productGroups.label: Travel sets for toilet, sewing or shoe cleaning
productGroups.blurb: Travel kits for personal toilet, sewing, or shoe or clothes cleaning pay 8.1% as a set; manicure and pedicure sets are in heading 8214.

productGroups.label: Buttons, snap fasteners, press studs & button blanks
productGroups.blurb: Snap fasteners pay 3.5% (up to 20¢ a dozen) or 2.7%; buttons of base metal or casein are Free; acrylic or polyester buttons pay a "line" rate — 0.3¢ per line per gross plus 4.6% (one line = 0.635 mm of button diameter); other plastic buttons 4.7%, pearl or shell 0.18¢/line/gross + 2.5%. Every 9606 line from China also pays +25% (List 3).

productGroups.label: Zippers (slide fasteners) & zipper parts
productGroups.blurb: Zippers with metal teeth pay 10%, with plastic teeth or coil 13%, and zipper parts (sliders, pulls, tape) 11.5%. Chinese zippers pay 47.5%–50.5% in total (List 3 + the 2026 Section 301 duty).

productGroups.label: Ballpoint pens, markers, fountain pens, mechanical pencils, refills & parts
productGroups.blurb: Ballpoint pens pay 0.8¢ each + 5.4%, markers and highlighters 4%, fountain and other pens and refills 0.4¢ each + 2.7%, mechanical pencils 6.6%. Pen and pencil sets (9608.50) pay the rate of each article as if entered separately. Nibs and most pen parts are Free.

productGroups.label: Pencils, crayons, pencil leads, pastels, chalk & charcoal
productGroups.blurb: Wood-cased pencils and crayons with a sheathed lead pay 14¢ per gross + 4.3%; pencil leads, wax crayons, pastels, chalk and charcoal are Free. Cased pencils from China also owe an antidumping duty of 114.90% (China-wide rate).

productGroups.label: Slates, chalkboards & whiteboards
productGroups.blurb: Chalkboards, whiteboards and slates with a writing or drawing surface pay 3.5%, framed or not.

productGroups.label: Hand stamps, date stamps & label embossers
productGroups.blurb: Hand-operated date, numbering and sealing stamps and hand label embossers pay 2.7%.

productGroups.label: Printer & typewriter ribbons, ink pads
productGroups.blurb: Ribbons under 30 mm in plastic or metal cartridges are Free; other printer ribbons, including thermal-transfer ribbons, pay 7.9%; ink pads 3.5%.

productGroups.label: Cigarette lighters, utility & multipurpose lighters, lighter parts
productGroups.blurb: Disposable gas lighters pay 4%, refillable pocket lighters 9%, table lighters 4.8%, electric and multipurpose (grill) lighters 3.9%, other lighters 8%–9%. Disposable, novelty and multipurpose lighters must be child-resistant under CPSC rules, and the importer must report each new model to CPSC 30 days before importing it.

productGroups.label: Smoking pipes, pipe bowls & cigar or cigarette holders
productGroups.blurb: Roughly shaped briar blocks are Free; wooden pipes 0.4¢ each + 3.2%, clay pipes 3%, glass and plastic pipes 0.3¢ each + 3.2%, metal holders 7.2%.

productGroups.label: Combs, hair clips, hairpins & hair curlers
productGroups.blurb: Plastic combs pay 14.4¢/gross + 2% (up to $4.50 a gross) or 28.8¢/gross + 4.6%; plastic hair clips and slides 5.3%; metal and other hair slides 11%; hairpins 5.1%; non-heated hair curlers 8.1%.

productGroups.label: Perfume atomizers & powder puffs
productGroups.blurb: Perfume atomizers and their mounts and heads are Free; powder puffs and cosmetic pads 4.3%.

productGroups.label: Vacuum flasks, insulated tumblers & bottles
productGroups.blurb: Vacuum flasks and vacuum-insulated tumblers and bottles up to 1 liter pay 7.2%, larger ones 6.9%, parts 7.2%. CBP classifies double-walled vacuum stainless-steel tumblers here (NY N356922). China supplied $1.30B of the $1.47B imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Mannequins, tailors' dummies & animated displays
productGroups.blurb: Tailors' dummies, display mannequins and animated shop-window displays pay 4.4%.

productGroups.label: Diapers, sanitary pads, tampons & incontinence products
productGroups.blurb: Diapers, sanitary pads and tampons of paper pulp, paper or cellulose wadding are Free; of plastics 5%; of textile wadding 3.6%–6.3%; cloth diapers and other textile articles 2.8%–16% by fiber. The largest heading by value: $1.95B in 2025, mostly Free-rated disposable products from Canada and Mexico.

productGroups.label: Tripods, monopods, bipods & similar supports
productGroups.blurb: Tripods and monopods of plastics pay 5.3%, of wood 3.3%, of iron or steel 2.9%, of aluminum 2.5%, of carbon fiber Free; accessories for binoculars (9005) and surveying instruments (9015) pay the rate of that instrument. Every 9620 line from China also pays +25% (List 3).

workedExamples.title: Stainless-steel vacuum tumbler from China (under 1 liter)
workedExamples.body: CBP classifies double-walled, vacuum-insulated stainless-steel tumblers as vacuum vessels (NY N356922): 7.2%. China adds +12.5% (9903.05.31); 9617.00.10 is on no list that is being collected (List 4B was suspended), so the total is **19.7%** — $1,970 on a $10,000 shipment. The same tumbler pays 19.7% from Vietnam or Thailand, 17.2% from Malaysia and nothing from Mexico under USMCA. Vessels over 2 liters (9617.00.40) are on List 4A: 26.9% from China.

workedExamples.title: Ballpoint pens from China vs. Japan
workedExamples.body: Ballpoint pens pay 0.8¢ each + 5.4%. For 10,000 pens worth $2,000 that is $80 + $108 = $188. From China add +12.5% (9903.05.31) and +7.5% (List 4A, 9903.88.15): $188 + $400 = **$588**, about 29% of the value. From Japan the 2026 Section 301 action charges 12.5% in total in place of a lower base rate (9903.05.49): **$250**. USMCA-qualifying pens from Mexico pay nothing.

workedExamples.title: Wood-cased pencils from China
workedExamples.body: The base rate is 14¢ per gross + 4.3%. On 1,000 gross (144,000 pencils) worth $10,000: $140 + $430. China adds +12.5% and +7.5% (List 4A): $2,000. And cased pencils from China are under an **antidumping duty order** since 1994: unless the exporter has its own rate, the cash deposit is the China-wide **114.90%** — $11,490. In all about **$14,060**, 141% of the value. The same pencils from Brazil pay $140 + 4.3% + 37.5% (Section 301 on Brazil) = $4,320.

workedExamples.title: Polyester buttons from China — the "line" rate
workedExamples.body: Buttons of acrylic or polyester resin pay 0.3¢ per line per gross + 4.6%. A "line" is 0.635 mm of button diameter (additional U.S. note 1), so a 24-line button (15.2 mm) pays 0.3¢ × 24 = 7.2¢ per gross of 144 buttons. On 1,000 gross worth $3,000: $72 + $138, plus +12.5% and +25% (List 3, 9903.88.03) = $1,125 — **$1,335** in all. The importer must report the line size so CBP can check the specific duty.

workedExamples.title: Pen-and-pencil gift set from Germany
workedExamples.body: A set of articles from two or more of 9608.10–9608.40 pays "the rate applicable to each article in the absence of this subheading": the ballpoint pen at 0.8¢ + 5.4% on its value, the mechanical pencil at 6.6% on its value. The importer gives each article's line and value. For EU goods the 2026 Section 301 action then charges 10% in total in place of a lower rate (9903.05.39), so a $10,000 shipment of German sets whose articles' own duty adds up to under 10% pays **$1,000**.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 96 — pens, pencils, brushes, buttons, zippers, lighters, vacuum flasks, diapers — since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 duties, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (Vietnam +12.5%, EU 10% in total), China List 3 and List 4A, the cased-pencil antidumping order, with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 96 base rate changed**: all 157 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates, from Free to 32%.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached these goods from every country — 19%–20% for Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia and Indonesia, 15% in total for EU and Japanese goods from August 2025, 50% for India from August 27, and up to 145% for China in April–May 2025 on top of its List 3 and List 4A duties. The IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff**: +10% for India, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia and the UK, +12.5% for Vietnam, Thailand and the Dominican Republic, 10% in total for the EU and Taiwan, 12.5% in total for Japan and Korea. China pays +12.5% plus its 2018–2019 list duty (+25% on buttons, zippers and tripods, +7.5% on most other lines). One aluminum-brush line lost its Section 232 duty on April 6, 2026, and the **antidumping order on cased pencils from China** (since 1994) stays at a China-wide 114.90%.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 96 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exemption for worked shell, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the China Section 301 List 3 and List 4A duties, the Section 232 aluminum duty that reached one brush line until April 2026 (and still reaches it for Russia), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. The Canada Section 338 duties name no Chapter 96 product. One antidumping order is in force — cased pencils from China (9609.10.00); the 1986 order on natural-bristle paint brushes from China was revoked in 2010. Preference programs (GSP, AGOA) are listed for reference. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

changes.title: No Chapter 96 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 157 Chapter 96 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition, and no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 and List 4A continue after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 96 this keeps +25% (List 3) on buttons, zippers and tripods and +7.5% (List 4A) on most pens, pencils, brooms, toothbrushes, lighters and diapers.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 lists revised; still no Chapter 96 product
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the 9903.03.12 and 9903.03.14 lists. None of the added or removed provisions is in Chapter 96.

changes.title: Cased pencils from China: preliminary review keeps the 114.90% rate
changes.detail: In the 2024–2025 administrative review of the antidumping order on cased pencils from China (9609.10.00), Commerce preliminarily found that the four reviewed exporters — Shanghai Yover, Yiwu Huijie, Zhejiang Pengsheng and Zhejiang Sinopencil — are part of the China-wide entity, whose 114.90% rate is not under review. Cash deposits stay at 114.90% until the final results.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duties take effect — no Chapter 96 product listed
changes.detail: The 50% duties on listed products of Canada (alcoholic beverages 9903.03.12, dairy 9903.03.13, motor-vehicle list 9903.03.14) apply even to USMCA goods, but none of the three lists names a Chapter 96 subheading, so Canadian diapers, brushes and pens pay no Section 338 duty.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover all of Chapter 96 but worked shell
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). Worked shell (9601.90.20) is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)); no other Chapter 96 line is, and no country exception list in note 52(j) names one. EU and Taiwan goods pay 10% in total and Japanese and Korean goods 12.5% in total (nothing extra on lines already that high). India, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia and the UK +10%; China, Vietnam, Thailand and the Dominican Republic +12.5%. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94).

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 96 line is on the Brazil exemption list (note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% forced-labor tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top: Brazilian pencils and crayons pay 14¢/gross + 41.8%.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still remove the base rate and the Section 301 duty on Canadian and Mexican Chapter 96 goods.

changes.title: Section 232 rebuilt: aluminum brushes and mops drop off the list
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the note 19 aluminum headings with the 9903.82 program and new product lists in U.S. note 16. 9603.90.80.50 is not on the new lists, so from April 6, 2026 it pays no Section 232 duty — except Russian goods, which still pay 200% (9903.85.68).

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 96 product was on the exemption list (9903.03.03) other than civil-aircraft tripods (9903.03.05). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. AGOA (SPI D) makes most dutiable Chapter 96 lines Free for eligible sub-Saharan countries, but not the textile diaper and pad lines (9619.00.21–9619.00.79) or printer ribbons (9612.10.90). changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not entered under CAFTA-DR will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025: 50% in all on Indian capsules, carvings and pencils, on top of the base rate. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025: Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand +19%, Vietnam +20%, India +25%, the UK +10%. EU goods with a column 1 rate under 15% paid 15% in total (9903.02.20); Japan (Executive Order 14345) and Korea got the same 15% in-total treatment later in 2025. Brazilian goods also paid 40% under Executive Order 14323. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10) from August 1, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum duty doubled to 50%
changes.detail: Proclamation 10947 raised the Section 232 aluminum duty from 25% to 50% (UK 25%), including on the aluminum content of 9603.90.80.50 brushes and mops. Ended for this line on April 6, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. A Chinese coil zipper then paid 13% + 25% (List 3) + 20% + 10% = 68% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025, and paused the higher country rates announced on April 2 for other countries (Vietnam 46%), which never took effect. With the 20% fentanyl duty and the 25% List 3 duty, a Chinese coil zipper paid 183% until May 13, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 96 product was on the exemption list (Annex II). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum duty reaches aluminum brushes and mops (9603.90.80.50)
changes.detail: Proclamation 10895 put 9603.90.80.50 (other brushes, brooms and mops — those with aluminum parts) on the derivative aluminum list of U.S. note 19(k): +25% on the aluminum content for every country from March 12, 2025 (9903.85.08), and +200% for products of Russia or with Russian-smelted or cast aluminum (9903.85.68). The general duty rose to 50% on June 4, 2025 and ended for this line on April 6, 2026; the Russian 200% continues.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the List 3 and List 4A duties. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10) from March 4, 2025, later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt from March 7, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China four-year review: no Chapter 96 increase
changes.detail: USTR raised Section 301 rates on Chinese steel and aluminum products, EVs, batteries, semiconductors, medical products and others (U.S. note 31, 9903.91.01–9903.91.11). No Chapter 96 line is on those lists, so buttons, zippers and tripods stay at +25% and the List 4A lines at +7.5%.

changes.title: Antidumping order on cased pencils from China continued
changes.detail: After the fifth five-year (sunset) review, Commerce and the ITC found that revoking the 1994 order would likely lead to continued dumping and injury, so the order on cased pencils from China (9609.10.00; mechanical pencils, crayons, pastels, charcoal and chalk excluded) stays in force. The next sunset review is due by 2028.

changes.title: China List 4A duty cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: Under the Phase One agreement USTR halved the List 4A duty (9903.88.15) from 15% to 7.5%, the rate still charged on 84 Chapter 96 lines.

changes.title: China List 4A reaches pens, pencils, brooms, lighters and diapers
changes.detail: The fourth China Section 301 list put +15% on Chinese pens, markers, pencils, crayons, brooms, toothbrushes, lighters, mannequins, large vacuum flasks, diapers and pads, capsules and carvings. List 4B (hairbrushes, paint brushes, combs, hair clips, small vacuum flasks and others) was suspended and never took effect.

changes.title: China List 3 duty raised to 25%
changes.detail: USTR raised the List 3 duty (9903.88.03) from 10% to 25%. In Chapter 96 List 3 covers every button and snap-fastener line (9606), every zipper line (9607) and every tripod and support line (9620).

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 reaches buttons, zippers and tripods
changes.detail: The third China Section 301 list put +10% on Chinese buttons, snap fasteners, button blanks, zippers and zipper parts, and tripods and similar supports.

changes.title: Antidumping order on paint brushes from China revoked
changes.detail: Commerce revoked the 1986 antidumping order on natural-bristle paint brushes and brush heads from China because the domestic industry no longer wanted it. Since then the only antidumping order on a Chapter 96 product is the one on cased pencils.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 96 goods were **$8.27B in 2025**, 9.1% less than the $9.10B of 2024 (the highest of the six years shown) but well above the $6.51B of 2020. The largest heading is **diapers, sanitary pads and tampons (9619), $1.95B** — up 4.0% and almost all from Canada ($888M), China ($467M) and Mexico ($290M). Next come **vacuum flasks and insulated tumblers (9617), $1.47B** (down 17.2%), of which China supplied $1.30B, then other brooms, brushes and mops (9603.90, $822M), **ballpoint pens ($441M) and markers ($417M)**, empty capsules and carvings (9602, $363M), toothbrushes ($312M) and makeup and artists' brushes ($289M). Loose buttons ($24M) and zippers ($32M) are small lines.

**China** supplied 49% — $4.08B, down 19.4% from $5.07B in 2024 as the 2025 IEEPA duties hit — and leads in flasks, brushes, combs, lighters and scent sprayers. **Vietnam** (+36.7% to $272M) and **Thailand** (more than doubled to $140M) grew fastest, mostly in brushes and vacuum flasks. **Canada** ($956M) and **Mexico** ($883M) together supplied 22%, mainly diapers and pads, plus Mexican pens, brushes and carvings; **Japan** ($279M) ships mainly pens and markers ($209M); Germany, France, Italy and Spain ship brushes, pens and lighters; **Brazil** ($69M) mostly pencils.

The figures are annual and stop at 2025, before the 2026 tariff changes (the end of the IEEPA duties in February and the Section 301 tariffs from July 24, 2026); they do not show what those changes did. Duty-collected figures are not available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Chapter 96 base rates are moderate — mostly 2%–10%, with many Free lines — so for most suppliers the **extra duty by country** is the bigger part of the bill. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — taken from the current tariff schedule.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** that started July 24, 2026: **+10% for India, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia and the UK**, **+12.5% for Vietnam, Thailand and the Dominican Republic**, **10% in total for EU and Taiwanese goods** and **12.5% in total for Japan and Korea** — nothing added where the base rate is already that high. **China adds 12.5% plus its list duty**: +25% on buttons, zippers and tripods, +7.5% on most pens, pencils, brooms, lighters and diapers, nothing more on combs, hair clips, paint brushes and small vacuum flasks. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico — including $1.18B of diapers and pads in 2025 — pay nothing. Brazil pays +37.5% on everything.

Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; P for Dominican Republic; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Not in the cells: the 114.90% antidumping duty on cased pencils from China (9609.10.00), which depends on the exporter and is collected as a cash deposit; the CPSC lighter rules and FDA device rules, which add compliance cost but no duty.

Sets and accessories (9608.50, 9620.00.15, 9620.00.30) take "the rate applicable" to another article; the cells show that wording plus the extra duty. For China the cells add the list duty of the set or accessory line; under notes 20(z)–(gg) (9903.88.21–9903.88.28) that list duty does not apply when the set or accessory takes its rate from a subheading that itself carries a China list duty.

Brooms of broomcorn (9603.10.05, 9603.10.40) pay 8% only until the year's quantity (61,655 dozen whiskbrooms, 121,478 dozen other brooms) has been entered; after that 5¢ or 32¢ each (9603.10.15, 9603.10.50). Each line is priced at its own rate.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. No Chapter 96 line is on the Canada Section 338 lists.

The Section 301 general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86) names one Chapter 96 line, worked shell (9601.90.20); the civil-aircraft list (note 52(d), 9903.05.88) names tripods of plastics and of carbon (9620.00.50, 9620.00.60) when entered for civil aircraft. No note 52(j) country exception list names a Chapter 96 line, and the CAFTA-DR textile relief (note 52(i)) is not applied to Chapter 96. The Brazil list (note 50(a)(ii)) has none. The Canada Section 338 lists (note 51(b)(1)–(3)) have none; 9620.00.50 and 9620.00.60 appear only on the civil-aircraft relief list (note 51(d)). China: List 3 (note 20(f)) covers all 9606, 9607 and 9620 lines; List 4A (note 20(r)/(s)) covers 84 lines; List 4B (note 20(u)) is suspended; the exclusions in force (notes 20(vvv), 20(www)) name no Chapter 96 product, and the older exclusions printed for mop heads, goat-hair lens brushes, liquid-chalk markers, spark lighters and steel tripods have expired; note 31 names none. Note 30(b) sets 35% for Russian 9603.10.90 in place of column 2. The temporary duty suspensions of subchapter II for hair slides, eyelash curlers, coffee servers and camera tripods (9902.17.95–9902.18.03) expired December 31, 2020. tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 96: Miscellaneous Manufactured Articles — Import Rules & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Pens, Lighters, Brushes & Diapers into the U.S.: CPSC Lighter Rules, FDA Tampon Rules, Pencil Antidumping & Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 96) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What each HTS Chapter 96 line needs at U.S. entry — CPSC child-resistance rules and 30-day reports for lighters, FDA device rules for tampons and pads, art-material labeling for crayons, the cased-pencil antidumping deposit, FWS rules for ivory and shell — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, origin, material and value brackets, broom quotas, FTAs, drawback and FTZs.
keywords: anti dumping on pencils from china

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 96 goods need no import license, but a few rules stop or delay shipments. **Lighters** must be child-resistant under CPSC standards (16 CFR parts 1210 and 1212), and the importer must report each new model to CPSC at least 30 days before importing it. **Tampons and menstrual pads** are FDA medical devices, so the foreign maker and the importer register and list with FDA. **Crayons, colored pencils, pastels and markers** are art materials that need ASTM D-4236 labeling, and children's versions need a Children's Product Certificate. **Cased pencils from China** owe a 114.90% antidumping deposit. **Ivory, tortoiseshell and coral** articles fall under Fish and Wildlife Service and CITES rules.

On cost, the base rate is usually small, so the levers are mostly about the **extra duty**: USMCA (every line Free, no Section 301 duty), where the goods are made (a coil zipper pays 50.5% from China, 25.5% from Vietnam), the material and unit value that set the line, the in-quota broom rate, FTAs, first-sale valuation, drawback and foreign-trade zones. Each lever depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on Canadian and Mexican goods
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 16%) and the 10% Section 301 duty — every dutiable Chapter 96 line is Free under USMCA (S)
levers.appliesTo: Diapers and pads, brushes, pens, pencils, carvings and other goods of Canada and Mexico that meet the USMCA rules of origin
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin (importer, exporter or producer) with the required data elements, and records supporting it.
levers.caveat: Goods that only pass through Canada or Mexico, or are made there from Chinese parts without the required tariff shift, do not qualify and pay the base rate + 10%. No Chapter 96 line is on the Canada Section 338 lists, so a valid claim leaves nothing to pay.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52

levers.title: Know the country of origin — where the article was made
levers.saves: The gap between country rates: on a ballpoint pen 0.8¢ each + 25.4% from China, + 17.9% from Vietnam, + 15.4% from India, 12.5% from Japan, 10% from the EU, Free from Mexico under USMCA; on a coil zipper 50.5% from China vs 25.5% from Vietnam
levers.appliesTo: All lines; the gap is widest on the China List 3 lines (buttons, zippers, tripods) and List 4A lines (pens, pencils, brooms, lighters, diapers)
levers.document: Production records showing where the article was made — for textile diapers and pads, where the fabric was formed or the article wholly assembled.
levers.caveat: For duty, origin is where the goods were last substantially transformed; packing, labeling or simple assembly in a third country does not change it. Textile articles of 9619.00.21–9619.00.79 follow the textile origin rules of 19 CFR 102.21. Antidumping duties follow the product: Commerce can find that pencils finished elsewhere from Chinese parts circumvent the order.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 52

levers.title: Cased pencils: source outside China or from an exporter with its own rate
levers.saves: The 114.90% antidumping cash deposit on wood-cased pencils from China (9609.10.00)
levers.appliesTo: Graphite and colored wood-cased pencils of 9609.10.00 from China; mechanical pencils, crayons, pastels, charcoal, chalk and novelty jumbo pencils are outside the order
levers.document: Proof of the country where the pencil was made (core encased), and for Chinese exporters a separate-rate determination in a Commerce administrative review.
levers.caveat: The China-wide rate applies to every Chinese exporter without its own rate; in the 2024–2025 review all four reviewed exporters were found part of the China-wide entity. The written scope, not the HTS number, decides coverage.

levers.title: Choose the material and type that carries the lower rate
levers.saves: Up to 16 points of base rate: diapers of paper pulp or cellulose wadding are Free, of plastics 5%, of synthetic textile 16%; buttons of base metal or casein Free vs 4.7% plastic; tripods of carbon fiber Free, aluminum 2.5%, plastics 5.3%; plastic hair slides 5.3% vs 11% for other materials
levers.appliesTo: Headings 9606, 9615, 9619 and 9620, where the rate follows the material
levers.document: A bill of materials with the material of each component and, for textile goods, the fiber content by weight.
levers.caveat: The goods must really be what the line describes; CBP classifies by what is imported, not by the invoice. A material change can also move a line onto or off a China list (paper diapers are on List 4A, some textile diapers on suspended List 4B).

levers.title: Declare unit values correctly — value brackets set the line
levers.saves: Several points where the rate depends on unit value: makeup and artists' brushes over 5¢ each are Free (2.6% below); hairbrushes over 40¢ pay 0.3¢ + 3.6% instead of 0.2¢ + 7%; combs over $4.50 a gross, snap fasteners over 20¢ a dozen and lighters over $5 a dozen each move to a different rate
levers.document: A commercial invoice with the per-unit price of each article, separate from cases, sets or packing.
levers.caveat: The value is the transaction value of the article as imported; splitting or bundling to cross a bracket is not allowed. Makeup brush sets with a case are classified as brushes when the brushes give the set its character (NY N342036).

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N342036 (makeup brush set)

levers.title: Enter broomcorn brooms while the in-quota rate is open
levers.saves: The difference between 8% and 32¢ each (or 32% over 96¢) on brooms of broomcorn, and 8% vs 5¢ each on whiskbrooms
levers.appliesTo: Brooms and whiskbrooms wholly or partly of broomcorn (9603.10.05–9603.10.60)
levers.document: Entry (or warehouse withdrawal) in the calendar year before 121,478 dozen brooms, or 61,655 dozen whiskbrooms, have been entered; CBP tracks how much has been entered.
levers.caveat: The quantity is filled first come, first served across all importers; once it is reached, the higher rate applies to the rest of the year. Brooms of other twigs pay 10%, and brooms of plastic fibers 2.8% (9603.90.80).

levers.title: Use an FTA, CAFTA-DR or AGOA for the base rate
levers.saves: The base rate — up to 16% — for goods of Korea, Israel, Australia, Colombia, Peru, the CAFTA-DR countries, other FTA partners and AGOA countries
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines with a Free special rate (all of them for most FTAs; AGOA leaves out the textile 9619 lines and printer ribbons)
levers.document: Proof that the goods meet the agreement's rules of origin: producer statements, bills of materials, production records.
levers.caveat: Under U.S. note 52(a) the 2026 Section 301 duty still applies when a special rate is claimed — Korean goods pay 12.5% in total, Dominican CAFTA-DR goods 12.5%. GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Value on the first sale for export
levers.saves: Duty on the middleman's markup — on every percentage rate and on the Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: Goods bought through a trading company or agent that bought them from the factory
levers.document: The factory invoice and proof that the first sale was for export to the United States at arm's length.
levers.caveat: Only a bona fide sale clearly destined for the United States qualifies; specific rates per piece, gross or line are not affected.

levers.title: American goods returned and assembly abroad
levers.saves: Duty on U.S. content: U.S.-made goods returned unchanged are Free (9801.00.10); articles assembled abroad from U.S. components pay duty only on the foreign value (9802.00.80)
levers.appliesTo: U.S. goods returned, and pens, lighters, brushes or tripods assembled abroad from U.S.-made parts
levers.document: Export records and the declarations in 19 CFR 10.1 (returns) or the documentation in 19 CFR 10.24 (assembly), with a breakdown of U.S. component values.
levers.caveat: The Section 301 duty still applies to the foreign value under 9802.00.80 (note 52(a)). Components that are further fabricated abroad, not just assembled, lose the allowance.

levers.title: Claim drawback on re-exported goods
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties, Section 301 duties included, on goods exported or used to make exported goods
levers.appliesTo: Imported pens, brushes, zippers, buttons and other goods that are re-exported, or used in exported products
levers.document: Import and export records linked by a drawback claim, filed in ACE within five years of import.
levers.caveat: Antidumping duties cannot be recovered through drawback, and substitution drawback needs goods of the same 8-digit subheading.

levers.title: Use a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: Deferral of duty on stock held in the zone, and no duty on goods re-exported from it
levers.appliesTo: Distribution stocks of pens, brushes, flasks and personal-care goods
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and an inventory-control system approved for the zone.
levers.caveat: Extra-duty notices can require privileged foreign status for goods admitted to a zone (the China Section 301 lists do), which fixes their classification and duty at admission; check the current Chapter 99 note before relying on zone status.

levers.title: Get a binding ruling
levers.saves: The risk of a wrong line: tumbler vs. vacuum flask, diaper material, brush type, set vs. separate articles, and the Chapter 99 numbers that go with it
levers.appliesTo: Any line where the material, the value bracket or the set rule is in doubt
levers.document: A ruling request with samples or photos, the material breakdown and the unit value.
levers.caveat: A ruling binds CBP only for the goods described; CBP has classified double-walled vacuum stainless tumblers in 9617.00.10 (NY N356922).

rules.title: Disposable and novelty cigarette lighters must resist operation by at least 85% of a test panel of children under 5 (16 CFR part 1210); the importer must send CPSC a report, with a sample, at least 30 days before first importing each model, and keep test records
Multipurpose (grill and fireplace) lighters must be child-resistant under 16 CFR part 1212, with the same 30-day report before import

A lighter filled with flammable gas may be offered for transport only if it holds no more than 10 grams of gas and its design has been examined and tested by a PHMSA-authorized testing agency, and it is packaged as the hazardous materials rules require

Products under a CPSC rule (lighters) need a General Certificate of Conformity, and children's products (children's crayons, pencils, hair clips) a Children's Product Certificate based on third-party testing — for lead content, among others; certificates must be eFiled with the entry from July 8, 2026
Art materials — crayons, colored pencils, pastels, chalk, drawing charcoal, markers — must be reviewed by a toxicologist and labeled under ASTM D-4236 (Labeling of Hazardous Art Materials Act)

Menstrual tampons and pads are medical devices: the foreign maker and the initial importer must register and list with FDA; tampons are Class II devices that need premarket notification (510(k)), most unscented pads are Class I and exempt; tampon labels must state absorbency and warn about toxic shock syndrome

Worked African elephant ivory cannot be imported except in narrow cases (musical instruments, exhibitions, household moves, inheritances); other wildlife articles — tortoiseshell, coral, horn, bone — need an FWS declaration and, for CITES species, permits; marine-mammal products such as whalebone and walrus ivory are prohibited

Cased pencils from China (9609.10.00) are subject to an antidumping order: the entry must be filed as an AD entry with the case number and a cash deposit (114.90% unless the exporter has its own rate)
Every article (or, where that is impossible, its container) must be marked with its country of origin in English
Textile diapers, pads and similar articles (9619.00.21–9619.00.79) take their origin from the textile rules: generally where the article is wholly assembled or the fabric formed

Report the right Chapter 99 numbers with the Chapter 96 line: the 2026 Section 301 heading for the country (9903.05.20–9903.05.84), 9903.05.86 for worked shell, 9903.05.93/.94 for USMCA goods, 9903.88.03 or 9903.88.15 for China, and 9903.88.21–9903.88.28 for sets and accessories that take another line's rate

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 52

groups.label: Worked ivory, bone, horn, shell, coral & mother-of-pearl
groups.note: Worked African elephant ivory is effectively barred; tortoiseshell, coral and horn need FWS clearance and CITES permits for listed species; whalebone and other marine-mammal products are prohibited. Worked shell is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty.

groups.label: Gelatin & vegetable capsules, wax figures, amber & other carvings
groups.note: No agency license for empty capsules or carvings. Capsules of gelatin (3%) and of vegetable cellulose (2.7%) have separate lines.

groups.label: Brooms, brushes, toothbrushes, makeup brushes, paint rollers & mops
groups.note: No agency license. The value per brush and the type (tooth, makeup, hair, paint) decide the line; broomcorn brooms have an annual in-quota quantity at 8%. Chinese paint brushes, rollers and hairbrushes carry no list duty (List 4B), Chinese toothbrushes and brooms +7.5%.

groups.label: Hand sieves & riddles
groups.note: No agency license.

groups.label: Travel sets for toilet, sewing or shoe cleaning
groups.note: Travel kits are classified as a set in 9605 at 8.1%, not article by article.

groups.label: Buttons, snap fasteners, press studs & button blanks
groups.note: Acrylic and polyester buttons pay a specific duty per line (0.635 mm) per gross: declare the line size. Every 9606 line from China pays +25% (List 3).

groups.label: Zippers (slide fasteners) & zipper parts
groups.note: No agency license. Every zipper line from China pays +25% (List 3) on top of 10%–13%.

groups.label: Ballpoint pens, markers, fountain pens, mechanical pencils, refills & parts
groups.note: Markers and other art pens are art materials (LHAMA labeling); pens for children need a Children's Product Certificate. Sets take each article's own rate.

groups.label: Pencils, crayons, pencil leads, pastels, chalk & charcoal
groups.note: Cased pencils from China owe the 114.90% antidumping deposit; crayons, pastels and chalk are art materials under LHAMA; children's pencils and crayons need a Children's Product Certificate.

groups.label: Slates, chalkboards & whiteboards
groups.note: No agency license.

groups.label: Hand stamps, date stamps & label embossers
groups.note: No agency license.

groups.label: Printer & typewriter ribbons, ink pads
groups.note: No agency license. Ribbons under 30 mm in cartridges are Free; other ribbons 7.9%.

groups.label: Cigarette lighters, utility & multipurpose lighters, lighter parts
groups.note: Disposable, novelty and multipurpose lighters must be child-resistant (16 CFR parts 1210, 1212) and reported to CPSC 30 days before the first import of each model; fuel-filled lighters need an approved design for transport.

groups.label: Smoking pipes, pipe bowls & cigar or cigarette holders
groups.note: No agency license for pipes and holders under customs rules; tobacco itself is chapter 24.

groups.label: Combs, hair clips, hairpins & hair curlers
groups.note: Hair clips and combs for children are children's products under CPSC rules.

groups.label: Perfume atomizers & powder puffs
groups.note: No agency license for sprayers and puffs; the cosmetics in them are FDA-regulated separately.

groups.label: Vacuum flasks, insulated tumblers & bottles
groups.note: No agency license. A tumbler that is double-walled and vacuum insulated is a vacuum vessel (9617.00.10, 7.2%).

groups.label: Mannequins, tailors' dummies & animated displays
groups.note: No agency license.

groups.label: Diapers, sanitary pads, tampons & incontinence products
groups.note: Tampons and menstrual pads are FDA medical devices (registration, listing, tampon labeling). Textile diapers and pads follow the textile origin rules. Paper-pulp diapers are Free from every country before the extra duty.

groups.label: Tripods, monopods, bipods & similar supports
groups.note: No agency license. Every 9620 line from China pays +25% (List 3); tripods of plastics or carbon for civil aircraft can skip the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(d)).

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 96 cover?
faqs.answer: Chapter 96 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, "Miscellaneous Manufactured Articles", has 157 tariff lines in 20 headings: worked ivory, bone and shell (9601), capsules and carvings (9602), brooms and brushes (9603), buttons (9606), zippers (9607), pens (9608), pencils and crayons (9609), boards, stamps and ribbons (9610–9612), lighters (9613), pipes (9614), combs and hair clips (9615), sprayers and powder puffs (9616), vacuum flasks (9617), mannequins (9618), diapers, sanitary pads and tampons (9619) and tripods (9620). The U.S. imported $8.27B of them in 2025.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for diapers, and are there tariffs on diapers?
faqs.answer: Baby and adult diapers are in heading 9619. Disposable diapers of paper pulp (9619.00.11) or of paper and cellulose wadding (9619.00.15.30) have a Free base rate; diapers of plastics pay 5% and cloth diapers 2.8%–16% by fiber. The extra duty depends on the country: nothing for USMCA-qualifying diapers from Canada and Mexico (which supplied $1.18B of heading 9619 in 2025), 10% in total from the EU, +12.5% from Vietnam or Thailand, and +20% from China (12.5% plus 7.5% List 4A) on paper diapers.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for sanitary pads and tampons, and what applies at import?
faqs.answer: Sanitary pads, panty liners and tampons of paper or cellulose wadding are 9619.00.15.10 (Free base rate); textile ones fall in 9619.00.21–9619.00.79. The extra duty follows the country, as for diapers: +20% from China, 10% in total from the EU, nothing for USMCA goods. Tampons and menstrual pads are also FDA medical devices: the maker and the initial importer register and list with FDA, tampons need premarket notification, and tampon labels must state absorbency and warn about toxic shock syndrome.

faqs.question: What is the HTS code and duty for pens?
searchedAs: hs code for pens and pencils
hs tariff code for ballpoint pen
faqs.answer: Ballpoint pens are 9608.10.00 (0.8¢ each + 5.4%), felt-tip pens and markers 9608.20.00 (4%), fountain and other pens 9608.30.00 (0.4¢ each + 2.7%), mechanical pencils 9608.40.40 (6.6%), ballpoint refills 9608.60.00 (0.4¢ each + 2.7%), and pen sets 9608.50.00 (each article at its own rate). On top: +20% from China, 12.5% in total from Japan, 10% in total from the EU, +12.5% from Vietnam; USMCA-qualifying pens from Mexico pay nothing.

faqs.question: Is there an antidumping duty on pencils from China?
searchedAs: anti dumping on pencils from china
faqs.answer: Yes. Wood-cased pencils from China (9609.10.00) have been under an antidumping order since December 1994, continued in March 2023. The China-wide cash deposit is 114.90% of the entered value, on top of the base rate (14¢ per gross + 4.3%) and the 20% Section 301 duties; Commerce's September 2026 preliminary review kept every reviewed exporter at that rate. Mechanical pencils (9608.40, 6.6%), crayons, pastels, charcoal and chalk are outside the order.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for lighters, and what rules apply?
faqs.answer: Disposable gas lighters are 9613.10.00 (4%), refillable gas pocket lighters 9613.20.00 (9%), table lighters 9613.80.10 (4.8%), electric and multipurpose grill lighters 9613.80.20 (3.9%), other lighters 9613.80.60–.80 (8%–9%). Chinese disposable lighters pay 24% in all; French or Spanish ones 10%. Disposable, novelty and multipurpose lighters must pass CPSC child-resistance tests, and the importer must report each model to CPSC 30 days before the first import.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code for a stainless-steel vacuum tumbler or flask?
faqs.answer: A double-walled, vacuum-insulated tumbler or bottle is a vacuum vessel of heading 9617 (CBP ruling NY N356922): 9617.00.10 (7.2%) up to 1 liter, 9617.00.30 (6.9%) for 1–2 liters, 9617.00.40 (6.9%) over 2 liters. From China add +12.5% — 19.7% or 19.4% in all — or +20% over 2 liters (List 4A); from Vietnam or Thailand +12.5%; from Mexico under USMCA nothing. A single-wall or non-vacuum steel tumbler is classified elsewhere.

faqs.question: What is the tariff code and duty for zippers?
faqs.answer: Zippers with metal teeth are 9607.11.00 (10%), with plastic teeth or coil 9607.19.00 (13%), and parts — sliders, pulls, heads — 9607.20.00 (11.5%). Every zipper line from China also pays +25% (List 3) and +12.5%, so Chinese zippers pay 47.5%–50.5%; from Vietnam 22.5%–25.5%, from Taiwan or the EU 10%–13%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for buttons?
faqs.answer: Buttons are heading 9606: of acrylic or polyester resin 9606.21.40 (0.3¢ per line per gross + 4.6%, where one line is 0.635 mm of diameter), other plastic buttons 9606.21.60 (4.7%), of base metal 9606.22.00 (Free), snap fasteners 9606.10 (2.7%–3.5%). Chinese buttons also pay +37.5% (List 3 plus the 2026 Section 301 duty).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for makeup brushes and toothbrushes?
searchedAs: hs code for makeup brush set
faqs.answer: Makeup brushes are 9603.30 — Free when valued over 5¢ each (2.6% at 5¢ or less); a set with a case stays there (CBP ruling NY N342036). Toothbrushes are 9603.21.00 (Free). Hairbrushes are 9603.29 (0.2¢ + 7% or 0.3¢ + 3.6%), paint brushes 9603.40.40 (4%), paint rollers 9603.40.20 (7.5%). From China, toothbrushes pay 20% and makeup brushes over 10¢ 12.5%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for combs and hair clips?
searchedAs: hs code for hair claw clip
hs code for hair bow clips
faqs.answer: Combs of plastics are 9615.11.10 (14.4¢ per gross + 2%, up to $4.50 a gross) or 9615.11.30 (28.8¢ per gross + 4.6%); plastic hair clips, claw clips and slides without imitation stones 9615.11.40 (5.3%); hair slides of other materials 9615.19.60 (11%); hairpins 9615.90.30 (5.1%). From China they pay only the 12.5% extra (no list duty).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a tripod or a mannequin?
faqs.answer: Tripods, monopods and bipods are heading 9620, by material: plastics 9620.00.50 (5.3%), wood 9620.00.55 (3.3%), carbon fiber 9620.00.60 (Free), iron or steel 9620.00.65 (2.9%), aluminum 9620.00.70 (2.5%). Chinese tripods pay +37.5% more. Mannequins and tailors' dummies are 9618.00.00 (4.4%); from China 24.4% in all.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for crayons and colored pencils?
faqs.answer: Colored pencils and crayons with a lead encased in a sheath are 9609.10.00 (14¢ per gross + 4.3%) — and wood-cased ones from China owe the 114.90% antidumping duty. Wax crayons, pastels and drawing charcoal not in a sheath are 9609.90.80 (Free). All are art materials that need ASTM D-4236 labeling, and children's ones a Children's Product Certificate.

faqs.question: How much tariff do Chapter 96 goods from China pay?
faqs.answer: Every line except worked shell pays +12.5% (9903.05.31) since July 24, 2026, on top of the base rate. Buttons, zippers and tripods add +25% (List 3); 84 lines — most pens, pencils, crayons, brooms, toothbrushes, lighters, mannequins and paper diapers — add +7.5% (List 4A); combs, hair clips, paint and hair brushes and vacuum flasks up to 2 liters add nothing. Cased pencils also owe 114.90% antidumping duty. The IEEPA duties, up to 145% in April–May 2025, ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Do Chapter 96 goods from Canada and Mexico pay tariffs?
faqs.answer: Not if they qualify for USMCA: every dutiable Chapter 96 line is Free under USMCA, and qualifying goods are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Non-qualifying goods pay the base rate + 10%. No Chapter 96 line is on the 50% Section 338 lists for Canada, and the 2025 IEEPA duties on both countries ended February 24, 2026.
